name: Bloom Energy
day_summary: Bloom Energy is trading at $326.19, up 1.31% (+$4.21) and pinned near its all-time high ($349.99 52-week high) after a wide $315.01–$345.50 session on 8.2M shares. The stock has become THE AI-data-center power trade of 2026 — up roughly 280% year-to-date from an $86.89 close at end-2025 — and today's grind higher near the record keeps the bulls firmly in control. The move is fundamental, not froth: an Oracle master agreement to procure up to 2.8GW of Bloom's solid-oxide fuel cells (1.2GW already contracted) to fully power the Project Jupiter AI campus in New Mexico, a $5B Brookfield partnership tied to AI infrastructure, and a backlog now in the $20–24B range. Bloom is the cleanest public expression of the thesis our Situational Awareness desk tracks — that the AI buildout is bottlenecked on power — and it is Aschenbrenner's single largest disclosed long.
long_pnl: Longs are sitting on a generational move — BE has run ~280% YTD and from a $21.50 52-week low to a $349.99 high — and added another 1.3% today near the record. Anyone in since the Oracle deal in April is up enormously; the only risk longs carry now is the altitude.
short_pnl: Shorts have been carried out all year; today's failed push to $345 and fade to $326 gave intraday faders a small scalp, but the structural short against a $20B+ backlog and raised guidance remains one of 2026's most painful trades.

decision.horizon: 1–2 quarters · into the Q2 FY26 print (~late July) and Oracle/Project Jupiter buildout milestones
decision.rationale: HOLD at medium conviction — own the flagship, don't chase the spike. The fundamental case is as strong as anything in the AI-power complex: a 2.8GW Oracle master agreement, a $5B Brookfield tie-up, a $20–24B backlog, Q1 revenue +130% to $751M, and raised FY26 guidance of $3.40–3.80B. Bloom sells on-site, fast-to-deploy baseload power exactly where the grid can't keep up — the literal bottleneck of the AI buildout. The catch is price: a ~$92.8B market cap on ~$3.5B of revenue is ~26x sales for a company that only just turned consistently profitable, after a ~280% run. New money should scale in on pullbacks toward the $290–$300 shelf rather than pay the record; existing holders ride the backlog but keep a trailing stop, because a name up 280% reprices violently on any execution wobble. As Aschenbrenner's top long, BE is the bellwether for the entire power-for-AI trade — watch it as a tell for the group.

A $20–24B backlog, the Oracle anchor, and Brookfield's capital give multi-year visibility. The bet is execution and margin: turning gigawatts of contracts into profitable, on-time deployments. analysis: Bloom Energy has completed a full identity change in 2026 — from a beaten-down clean-energy name to the marquee AI-data-center power trade — and the stock's ~280% run reflects it. The investment case is unusually clean: AI data centers need gigawatts of power faster than the grid can deliver, and Bloom's solid-oxide fuel cells are one of the few solutions that install on-site in months. The Oracle 2.8GW master agreement, the $5B Brookfield partnership, and a $20–24B backlog turn that narrative into contracted revenue. This is precisely the bottleneck our Situational Awareness desk argues the AI buildout runs into first, and it is why Bloom is Aschenbrenner's largest disclosed long. The only real debate is price: at ~26x sales near an all-time high, the easy money has been made, and the next leg depends on converting backlog to profitable deployments rather than on more headlines. Hold it as the flagship of the power-for-AI thesis, add on pullbacks toward $300, and treat its tape as the group's bellwether.
